text: Five persons P, Q, R, S and T sit in a row facing north. P sits at the extreme left end. Q sits immediately to the right of P. R sits at the extreme right end. S sits immediately to the left of R. Who sits in the middle?
explanation: The seats are 1 P, 2 Q, 4 S and 5 R. So T takes seat 3, which is the middle.

text: In a row of 40 students, Ravi is 12th from the left and Mohan is 18th from the right. How many students are between them?
explanation: Mohan is 40 - 18 + 1 = 23rd from the left. The students between them are 23 - 12 - 1 = 10.

text: Four friends A, B, C and D sit around a circular table facing the centre. A sits opposite C. B sits immediately to the right of A. Who sits immediately to the left of A?
explanation: The two seats beside A are taken by B and D, because C is opposite. B is on the right, so D is on the left.

text: P, Q, R, S and T live on different floors of a five-floor building, numbered 1 (lowest) to 5. S lives on the top floor and T on the lowest floor. R lives on the floor immediately below Q. P lives above Q. Who lives on the third floor?
explanation: S is on 5 and T on 1. P, Q and R share floors 2, 3 and 4. P is above Q, so Q cannot be on 4. R is directly below Q, so Q is on 3, R on 2 and P on 4.

text: Five lectures are held from Monday to Friday, one each day. Physics is on Tuesday. Chemistry is on the day after Physics. Maths is held before Physics. English is on Friday. On which day is Biology held?
explanation: Physics is on Tuesday and Chemistry on Wednesday. Maths must be before Tuesday, so it is on Monday. English is on Friday, which leaves Thursday for Biology.

text: Statements: A > B, B > C. Conclusions: I. A > C. II. C > A.
explanation: A is greater than B and B is greater than C, so A is greater than C. II is the opposite, so it is false.

text: Statements: P >= Q, Q > R. Conclusions: I. P > R. II. P = R.
explanation: P >= Q and Q > R, so P is strictly greater than R. P = R cannot be true.

text: Statements: X < Y, Y <= Z. Conclusions: I. X < Z. II. X <= Z.
explanation: X is less than Y, and Y is at most Z, so X is less than Z. If X < Z is true, then X <= Z is also true, so both follow.

text: A machine adds 3 to the input and then doubles the result. If the input is 7, what is the output?
explanation: First add 3: 7 + 3 = 10. Then double it: 10 x 2 = 20.

text: What is the age of Ravi? I. Ravi is 4 years older than Sita. II. Sita is 20 years old.
options: I and II together are needed
Even I and II together are not sufficient
explanation: I gives only the difference in ages and II gives only Sita's age. Together, Ravi is 20 + 4 = 24.

text: Is the whole number x even? I. x is divisible by 4. II. x is a prime number.
options: I alone is sufficient but II alone is not
II alone is sufficient but I alone is not
Either I or II alone is sufficient
Neither I nor II is sufficient
explanation: Every number divisible by 4 is even, so I settles it. A prime can be 2 (even) or 3 (odd), so II alone does not.
